title: African silhouettes, production markers and grading

say: African silhouettes, production markers, and grading.
This is the video for module four of Advanced Tailoring and Pattern Making.
You will draft iro and buba, kaftans and boubous, and calculate fabric before you buy.

say: A kimono-cut buba is a T-shape, with the sleeve cut in one with the body. For example, Yetunde in Abeokuta drafts for a client with a 104 cm bust. She chooses 20 cm of ease, so each quarter is 31 cm at bust level.

panel.heading: Yetunde drafts a buba and iro
items: Bust 104 + 20 ease, ÷ 4 = 31 cm a quarter
Hip check: (112 + 8) ÷ 4 = 30 cm, so fine
Closer sleeve: 10 cm bias gusset
Iro: 4 cm waistband, 25 cm front overlap
Hooks and bars so it stays for dancing

say: She checks the hip: 112 plus 8, divided by 4, needs 30 cm. Her 31 cm side line is enough, so the side seam runs straight.

panel.heading: Yetunde drafts a buba and iro
items: Bust 104 + 20 ease, ÷ 4 = 31 cm a quarter
Hip check: (112 + 8) ÷ 4 = 30 cm, so fine
Closer sleeve: 10 cm bias gusset
Iro: 4 cm waistband, 25 cm front overlap
Hooks and bars so it stays for dancing

say: The client wants a closer sleeve, which can pull up and tear at the underarm. So Yetunde adds a bias-cut gusset of 10 cm by 10 cm at each underarm.

panel.heading: Yetunde drafts a buba and iro
items: Bust 104 + 20 ease, ÷ 4 = 31 cm a quarter
Hip check: (112 + 8) ÷ 4 = 30 cm, so fine
Closer sleeve: 10 cm bias gusset
Iro: 4 cm waistband, 25 cm front overlap
Hooks and bars so it stays for dancing

say: For the iro, she adds a 4 cm waistband with a 25 cm front overlap and two hooks and bars, so it stays secure but still looks like a wrapper.

panel.heading: Yetunde drafts a buba and iro
items: Bust 104 + 20 ease, ÷ 4 = 31 cm a quarter

say: She tests the buba in calico and asks the client to lift both arms and dance a few steps.

say: A boubou is built from rectangles folded at the shoulder, spanning wrist to wrist. Check fabric width first. For example, Hadiza in Kano has a client with an arm span of 158 cm, but her fabric is only 116 cm wide.

panel.heading: Hadiza plans a boubou
items: Arm span 158 cm, fabric 116 cm wide
Shortfall 42 cm: two side panels
Length: 2 × 138 + hems = 282 cm
Total: 564 cm, about 5.64 m
6 yards is short, so buy 7 yards

say: The shortfall is 42 cm, so she adds two symmetrical side panels, each 24 cm wide with seam allowance.

panel.heading: Hadiza plans a boubou
items: Arm span 158 cm, fabric 116 cm wide
Shortfall 42 cm: two side panels
Length: 2 × 138 + hems = 282 cm
Total: 564 cm, about 5.64 m
6 yards is short, so buy 7 yards

say: The centre panel is 2 times 138, plus 3 cm hem at each end. That is 282 cm. The side panels fit side by side in one more length.

panel.heading: Hadiza plans a boubou
items: Arm span 158 cm, fabric 116 cm wide
Shortfall 42 cm: two side panels
Length: 2 × 138 + hems = 282 cm
Total: 564 cm, about 5.64 m
6 yards is short, so buy 7 yards

say: So she needs 564 cm, about 5.64 m, plus some for facing and print matching.

panel.heading: Hadiza plans a boubou
items: Arm span 158 cm, fabric 116 cm wide

Length: 2 × 138 + hems = 282 cm
Total: 564 cm, about 5.64 m
6 yards is short, so buy 7 yards

say: 6 yards is only about 5.49 m, which is not enough, so she buys 7. One yard is 0.9144 m, so always convert carefully.

say: Each skirt now uses 1.2 m instead of 1.4, so 20 skirts save 4 m. But only turn pieces on plain fabric with no nap. Never on a one-way print or velvet.

say: A marker is the layout of all pieces on the fabric. For example, Rukayat in Ilorin cuts choir skirts. Each skirt's pieces total about 1.5 square metres, on 1.5 m wide fabric.

cards.d: Close or guard rotary and electric cutters every time you put them down.
Cut away from your body. Keep your other hand flat and well away from the cutting line.
Never leave blades where children can reach them.

say: Cut away from your body, and keep your other hand flat and well away from the cutting line. Start with a small number of layers, because the blade drifts and lower pieces come out bigger.

cards.d: Close or guard rotary and electric cutters every time you put them down.

Never leave blades where children can reach them.

say: Rotary cutters and electric cloth cutters are very sharp. Close or guard the blade every time you put it down.

panel.heading: Tola grades her buba, M to XL
items: Bust interval 5 cm ÷ 4 = 1.25 cm a quarter
M to XL is two sizes: 2.5 cm out
Length: 1 cm per size, XL 2 cm longer
Nest the sizes: lines evenly spaced
Sew the XL in calico first

say: Cut away from your body, with your other hand flat and well away from the line. Start with few layers, because the blade drifts.

say: To remember. Ease and the underarm curve shape the buba. Check fabric width and convert yards carefully. Nest pieces only on fabric with no nap.
Guard every blade, and test the largest graded size.
